checks: Independently recomputed Xb4d native 3-2 HCN/HCO+ (team/checks/c_q1.py: own cube read, 7x7 local baseline, |v-2780|<350 km/s, peak of box): N 0.88, S 0.41, Bridge 0.50 (centre-pixel 0.48). Worker: N 0.88-0.90, S 0.39-0.40, Bridge 0.48-0.50. AGREE (<=3%). The K/Jy factor 1.0126 = (nu_HCO+/nu_HCN)^2 is correct.

Read s30 outputs: the numbers in the work summary tables match s30_ratios.txt. Convention (matched circular beams, same velocity window, fixed positions, same dv) is standard and stated. Ratios are insensitive to the 250/500/350 km/s window (<3%).

Nuclear result is credible: N R(3-2) rises 0.60 -> 0.90 -> 1.03 as the beam goes 5.7x3.5'' -> 0.94'' -> 0.25'', while S stays 0.38-0.48, so S/N ~0.45-0.6 at resolved scale. 'S is not enhanced relative to N' holds. Note the resolved N/S ratio is much more contrasted than the blended 6.5'' values: the 6.5''/10'' R(2-1), R(4-3) nuclear numbers are 15-20% cross-contaminated and the headline S/N ~0.6-0.75 there is diluted.

Disagree that the disk ratio is 'not measurable'. In the s30 output Xb55 (Band 5, 2-1, the best-behaved extended-emission array) gives a positive 8<r<20'' annulus with R = 0.30+-0.01 (HCN 5.4, HCO+ 17.7 Jy km/s), vs 0.56 inside r<8'' - a factor ~2 drop that bears directly on the 'active region vs disk' question. This was not reported or discussed. Xb4d gives a positive annulus R=0.58+-0.04 while Xb4f gives NEGATIVE fluxes (-9, +1.8) in the same annulus: the signs disagree between arrays, so the annulus is dominated by bowl/cleaning/pb-noise, not 'disk' emission. Also, Band 6 pbcor at r=12-20'' (12-m primary beam ~24'' FWHM at 265 GHz, PB 0.5-0.2) is not in the error budget, only the Band 7 case is mentioned.

Deblending (s31): a single zone template taken from Xb4d 3-2 (which line? appears HCO+/HCN-integrated) is used for both HCN and HCO+ at J=2 and 4. The zones themselves differ in HCN/HCO+ (N 0.56 vs S 0.375 vs Ext 0.71), so the template for HCN must differ from that for HCO+. chi2_red 35-240 shows the model does not describe the maps; the 'Ext' coefficient fits to exactly 0.000 in every fit (hard bound, suspicious), and N/S coefficients are anticorrelated at -0.5 to -0.7. The 3-2 self-check works only because the templates were derived from the same 3-2 data. The quoted +-0.05 are not credible for the 10'' R(2-1)/R(4-3) of S. I treat N/S ladder values as qualitative only.

Sblue wing (s32): methodology (fixed aperture, noise from 400 line-free random positions, matched beams) is much better than team-a's per-line peak pixel. But the significance is overstated. Wing R = 1.43+-0.33 vs core at the SAME position 0.61+-0.13 differs by 0.82+-0.35 = 2.3 sigma, not 3; vs the S-nucleus core (0.38+-0.02) it is 3.1 sigma but that compares a different position/kinematic component. HCN and HCO+ wing detections are 6.9 and 5.4 sigma in a small (sub-beam) aperture with pixel-correlated noise; the ratio of two noisy positives is biased high and the error is symmetric Gaussian. Aperture centre uncertainty (+-0.2'') was only noted. The N-nucleus red wing gives HCN 0.10 vs HCO+ 0.016 (R~6) at ~3 sigma, which shows that at this noise level apparent extreme wing ratios happen at random/blended positions: a null test is needed. The statement that team-a's 1.8 is 'biased high' is asserted, not demonstrated.

Not checked / cannot confirm: that the wing is not a blend (neighbouring lines within -400..-150 km/s of HCN 3-2 and HCO+ 3-2 were not listed in the Q1 summary; HCN-vib 4-3 is only ~400 km/s from HCO+ 4-3, relevant for the J=4 windows and for the 500 km/s test).

fixes.what: Report a disk ratio and the radial trend HCN/HCO+ vs radius at J=2-1 (Xb55) and a clean statement for J=3-2 and 4-3, with a go/no-go test for each.
fixes.why: The question asks for the disk explicitly, and the data already show a positive Xb55 annulus ratio of 0.30 (2-1) vs 0.56 inside r<8''. The 'resolved-out bowl' argument applies to Band 6/7 compact arrays, not (equally) to Band 5, and the Xb4d vs Xb4f annulus signs disagree, which is evidence of artefacts, not of absent measurability.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use annuli/sectors and the clumps E1/E2/W at a common 10'' beam for Xb55, Xb4f, Xb4d, Xb47; apply PB correction explicitly (model the 12-m beam at each band, mask where PB<0.5, propagate the noise 1/PB). Test whether the annulus is trustworthy by comparing flux of each array in the same annulus with the mfs continuum and with CO-like extended proxies, and by measuring the zero-level (negative bowl) from empty-sky regions at the same radius in line-free channels. Report the disk ratio only from arrays where the annulus flux is positive and consistent, with the (R_disk vs R_nucleus) difference and its uncertainty; otherwise give a lower/upper limit. Quote the Xb55 0.30 as a (conditional) result and discuss its consequence: HCN/HCO+ lower in disk/clumps than in nuclei, consistent with Harada 2018's finding that nuclei are not special but spiral arms differ. Cross-check with Ledger+2021 (HCN 3-2/1-0 ~0.3-0.4 in NGC 3256) as ladder-slope context.

fixes.what: Redo the N/S ladder deblend with line-specific templates and a model that fits.
fixes.why: One template for both lines, chi2_red 35-240, Ext fixed to 0, and 0.5-0.7 correlation between coefficients: current N/S R(2-1) and R(4-3) values and their errors are not trustworthy. They are the numbers that go into Q3.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Build separate N, S, Bridge, Ext templates for HCN and HCO+ from the Xb4d (or Xb4b-smoothed) cubes of that very line, convolve each exactly to the Band 5/6/7 beam (use the per-channel beams; Fourier convolution with the true kernel and pixel regridding), then fit one scale per zone per J with a free baseline (bowl) term and with an Ext term allowed to go negative in the covariance, and include the template-shape error by bootstrapping the template (shift +-0.2'', rescale +-10%) and by cross-array filtering recovery (p0003). Report posteriors including the N-S anti-correlation, and give the 2-1/3-2 and 4-3/3-2 ladder ratios per zone (the quantity needed for Q3), not just R(J). Validate by injection: build a synthetic J=2 or 4 map from the Xb4d 3-2 maps with known zone ladder ratios, convolve, add noise, refit.

fixes.what: Calibrate the Sblue wing claim: null test, significance on the ratio, robustness, and an explicit statement of the consequence of each interpretation.
fixes.why: R=1.4 +- 0.3 at a sub-beam aperture from two ~5-7 sigma detections is the highest-impact claim (outflow enhancement) and rests on a 2.3-3 sigma difference. N-nucleus red-wing R~6 is an example that unlikely-looking ratios occur.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: (1) Null test: apply the identical pipeline (aperture, windows, per-pixel baseline) to the 400 random line-free positions AND to bright positions with matched wing windows (N, S, Bridge, Ext) and report the distribution of wing R and its false-positive rate at R>1.2. (2) Compute the ratio posterior (ratio of correlated Gaussians or MCMC on the two fluxes with positivity), give 68/95% intervals and a lower limit on R_wing - R_core. (3) Vary the wing window (e.g. -350..-100, -300..-200, -450..-150) and aperture centre by +-0.2'' and show the spectrum of both lines at the blob (beam spectrum at the peak and aperture spectrum) so the wing is visible as an actual separate kinematic component, not the tail of the core. (4) Repeat with Xb4b smoothed to the Xb4d beam (independent array) as a replication, and with Xb4f for the integrated wing. (5) List neighbouring lines in the wing windows. (6) Reproduce p0001's 1.8+-0.3 by applying their 'peak pixel per line' recipe to the noise positions to show the bias, or drop the bias statement. (7) Derive consequences: with R_K~1.4 and optically thin 3-2, N(HCN)/N(HCO+) vs excitation: at the density where RADEX (s33) gives R(3-2) ~0.4 at the nuclei, what abundance ratio is needed for 1.4, and does it need shock/high-T chemistry (cf. Nishimura+2024 outflow HCN/HCO+ enhancement; Harada+2018 no AGN enhancement)? Label as tentative.

fixes.what: Show the HCN/HCO+ ratio map and radial/azimuthal profile of the 3-2 ratio at 0.94'' and 0.25'' with S/N cut, and quote the ratio of the integrated S-nucleus emission within the S aperture vs outflow-lobe region (not only a blob).
fixes.why: The headline is 'S is not enhanced, N is'. At the highest resolution the N ratio exceeds 1, a trend with resolution that suggests a compact HCN-bright core (AGN-like) in N, not S. This should be quantified and tested (centroid offsets, significance) because it reverses the naive AGN expectation and needs checking against continuum positions.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Pixel-by-pixel ratio map at matched 0.94'' (Xb4d) with a 5-sigma cut in both lines, then Xb4b convolved to the same beam as a replication; quote the ratio within concentric 0.25-0.5-1-2'' apertures about each continuum peak with matched apertures, and compare with the 0.25'' native Xb4b values to show beam dilution rather than filtering (p0003). Discuss whether the N excess could reflect HCN-vib contamination or HCN opacity (point to Q4).

fixes.what: State the sensitivity of every Q1 headline number to the cross-band systematic and to the beam-matching/regridding method, and update report.json accordingly.
fixes.why: Matched-J ratios are within one band, so calibration cancels, but the ladder ratios R(2-1):R(3-2):R(4-3) across Bands 5/6/7 depend on flux scale (10-35% per p0003) and on Xb4f/Xb47 recovery. The summary says p0003's recovery was not applied to these ratios; that is fine for within-band R(J) but must be stated as not valid for the ladder-slope statements (the 'fall by 25% per J step' etc.).
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Separate in the report within-band R(J) (calibration-free, 5% HCN/HCO+ systematic) from cross-band ladder slopes (add the 10-35% systematic). Compare Xb4f vs Xb47/Xb55 at a shared 10'' beam for a line pair at an overlapping J (e.g. CS or CH3OH lines in common) before quoting ladder slopes.

notes_for_questioner: (1) New: Band 5 shows R(2-1) falling from 0.56 inside r<8'' to 0.30 in 8-20'' (and clumps E1/E2/W 0.5 at 10''), so HCN/HCO+ may drop by ~2 in the disk; add a sub-question on whether this is a real disk/clump ratio vs resolved-out bowl, and the density/abundance implication. (2) At 0.25'' N has HCN>=HCO+ (1.03); ask what compact N component this is (continuum, velocity width, HCN-vib) and whether it is an AGN-like hidden nucleus in the 'starburst' nucleus. (3) Sblue wing: only HCN/HCO+ 3-2 are available at the resolution needed, so the abundance-vs-excitation degeneracy cannot be broken there; ask whether CS 7-6/SO/H13CN in Band 7 give anything at the 4'' scale for the whole S outflow (Q4/Q9). (4) The N 'red wing' HCN excess (HCN 0.1 vs HCO+ 0.016 Jy km/s) is odd; either a blend or an inflow/second component - ask Q0/Q2 to check line identification.
